title: Letterboxd
summary: A list, a rating, and one sentence. The one sentence is the platform's whole register.

larp.dek: The canon is public, the reviews are free, and nobody can audit whether you watched it.

crib.heading: References
lines: Jeanne Dielman. The 2022 Sight & Sound number one.
Tsai Ming-liang. Long takes, little dialogue.
Wong Kar-wai. Everyone has seen it, few have rewatched it.
Four and a half is the ceiling. Five is a personality statement.

crib.heading: Opinions to hold
lines: The letterboxing joke is old and you are past it.
You log rewatches, which is the mark of an account in use.
Any director's consensus favourite is their third best.

phrases.line: I need a rewatch before I rate it.
phrases.when: Asked for a star rating you do not have.

phrases.line: Four and a half. I don't give fives.
phrases.when: Asked about something you did like. Withholding the fifth star is the whole register.

phrases.line: I watched it on a Tuesday and it did nothing for me.
phrases.when: Asked about a film everybody loves. Indifference is unfalsifiable.

surface: A list, a rating, and one sentence. The one sentence is the platform's whole register.
Never write a paragraph. The form is a caption and length reads as effort, which reads as new.

follow_up.question: "What have you actually watched this month?"
follow_up.why: Larpers have a canon. Users have a recent history, and a real one is full of mediocre films watched on a Tuesday for no reason.

counter.move: Name something ordinary and slightly bad that you watched on a weeknight for no reason. A mediocre film is far more convincing than a masterpiece, because nobody's real month is a curated list.
counter.holds: Indefinitely. There is nothing here anybody can check.

tells: Every favourite is above four stars. Real accounts have a two-star film they will defend at length.
No rewatches. Nobody who loves film watches everything exactly once.
You talk about films. Users talk about watching films, which is a different subject with different sentences.
cost: None. There is no one to catch you, and that is the finding rather than an oversight.
The only exposure is to yourself, eventually, in a conversation with someone who has seen it.

learn.make: Log twenty films you have already seen, honestly, including the bad ones.

key_people: Chantal Akerman. Jeanne Dielman topping the 2022 Sight & Sound poll reset what the canon signals.
Wong Kar-wai. Universally admired, rarely rewatched, and safe to praise.
Tsai Ming-liang and Bela Tarr. The long-take directors people name to signal patience.
The Sight & Sound poll itself, which is the closest thing the site has to scripture.
timeline: 2011: Letterboxd launches, and film logging becomes a public activity.
2020: lockdown roughly triples the userbase and the register settles into the one-line review.
2022: Jeanne Dielman displaces Vertigo, and the discourse about it runs for a year.
